subject: Chemistry
description: Group 1 alkali metals + Group 2 alkaline earth — properties, reactivity, key compounds

questions.stem: s-BLOCK consists of which periodic groups?
questions.explanation: s-BLOCK = elements where the LAST valence electron enters s-orbital. GROUP 1 = ALKALI METALS (H, Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs, Fr); 1 valence electron, +1 oxidation state. GROUP 2 = ALKALINE EARTH METALS (Be, Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba, Ra); 2 valence electrons, +2 oxidation state. H is technically Group 1 by configuration but behaves differently (covalent, gaseous, etc.). REACTIVITY INCREASES down the group (atomic radius increases, ionization energy decreases).

questions.stem: Why are SODIUM (Na) and POTASSIUM (K) stored under KEROSENE OIL?

options.option_text: To prevent reaction with air + moisture
To make them magnetic in nature here
To slow down their natural radioactivity

questions.explanation: Alkali metals (Na, K, Cs, Rb) — extremely REACTIVE: react with air's oxygen + moisture. Reaction with water: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂↑ (exothermic; can ignite the H₂; K reaction even more violent — purple flame; Cs nearly explosive). Stored under kerosene (or paraffin oil) — these are non-polar, don't react with metals. Distractor 4 — Na, K not radioactive (Fr is, but rare).

questions.explanation: Table SALT = sodium chloride NaCl. Mainly from sea evaporation (India: Gujarat, Tamil Nadu coastlines), rock salt mines (Khewra, Pakistan; Cheshire, UK). IODISED salt (1924+): KI / KIO₃ added to prevent iodine deficiency (goitre, mental retardation). Distractor 1 = WASHING SODA (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O). Distractor 3 = BAKING SODA (NaHCO₃, also antacid). Distractor 4 = GLAUBER'S SALT (Na₂SO₄·10H₂O).

questions.stem: GYPSUM (used in plaster of paris) chemically is:
questions.explanation: GYPSUM = CaSO₄·2H₂O. PLASTER OF PARIS (POP) = CaSO₄·½H₂O — formed by heating gypsum to ~150°C (loses 1.5 of 2 H₂O). When mixed with water, sets back to gypsum + hardens — used in casts, ceiling, sculpture. Other Ca compounds: LIMESTONE / MARBLE / CHALK = CaCO₃; QUICKLIME = CaO; SLAKED LIME = Ca(OH)₂; BLEACHING POWDER = Ca(OCl)Cl. India: Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat are major gypsum producers.

questions.stem: Which alkaline earth metal is MOST important for HUMAN BONES + TEETH?
questions.explanation: CALCIUM (Ca) — major mineral in BONES (~99% of body's Ca) + TEETH (as hydroxyapatite — Ca₅(PO₄)₃(OH)). Also crucial for: muscle contraction (including heart), nerve signaling, blood clotting. RDA ~1000 mg/day adult. Sources: milk, yogurt, cheese, leafy greens, fish bones (sardines), tofu, ragi. DEFICIENCY → osteoporosis (esp. post-menopausal women), rickets in children, muscle cramps. MAGNESIUM (Mg) also in bones (~25 g body Mg) but less. CHLOROPHYLL has Mg at center (like Fe in haemoglobin). Distractor 4 — Barium is TOXIC; used in BaSO₄ for X-ray contrast (insoluble = safe).

questions.stem: FLAME TEST: which alkali metal gives a CRIMSON RED flame?
questions.explanation: FLAME TESTS — characteristic colours from electronic transitions when metal salts heated: LITHIUM (Li) = crimson/red; SODIUM (Na) = bright yellow (most common, very intense); POTASSIUM (K) = lilac/purple; RUBIDIUM (Rb) = red-violet; CESIUM (Cs) = blue. Group 2: CALCIUM (Ca) = brick red; STRONTIUM (Sr) = crimson; BARIUM (Ba) = pale green; COPPER (Cu) = blue-green. Used in classroom QUALITATIVE analysis. Fireworks COLOURS use this principle: Sr salts → red, Cu → green/blue, Na → yellow, K → purple, Ba → green.

questions.stem: WASHING SODA (used in cleaning) is chemically:
questions.explanation: WASHING SODA = sodium carbonate decahydrate (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O). Mildly basic (pH ~11) → softens hard water (binds Ca²⁺ + Mg²⁺), removes greasy stains. Made by SOLVAY process (NH₃ + CO₂ + NaCl + H₂O → NaHCO₃ + NH₄Cl; heat NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂). BAKING SODA (NaHCO₃) — milder; used in cooking + as antacid + fire extinguishers. CAUSTIC SODA (NaOH) — very strong base; soap-making (saponification), paper, drain cleaners. CHLOR-ALKALI process (electrolysis of brine) produces NaOH, Cl₂, H₂.
